subject.title: feat(config): use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numeric `.bak.N` recovery points during migration, or may first-run cleanup delete them?
rationale: Config backups may be the user's only rollback copy, and repository policy treats config recovery and migration behavior as compatibility-sensitive rather than automation-only.

options.title: Preserve or convert legacy backups
options.body: Require the linked PR or replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files through migration or fold them into the new timestamped retention set without silently deleting useful recovery points.

options.title: Accept legacy cleanup
options.body: Allow first-run cleanup to delete numbered backups, but document that upgrade behavior and require proof that the remaining recovery path is acceptable.

options.title: Keep the numeric ring
options.body: Reject the timestamped naming change for now and keep the current numbered backup ring as the supported behavior.

recommendation.title: Preserve or convert legacy backups
recommendation.body: Require the linked PR or replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files through migration or fold them into the new timestamped retention set without silently deleting useful recovery points.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history for config backup, recovery, and tests points to steipete as the best available owner for this upgrade-behavior choice.
